title: Fiume, 1626
eyebrow: Rijeka · a household a hundred and thirteen years too early
dek: Giovanni Kobler went through the civic records of Fiume in the 1870s and wrote out for Carlo De Franceschi every household of this surname he could find. His earliest is «Valentino Defranceschi, venuto dalla Carnia, fu fatto Cittadino nel 1739» — come from Carnia, made a citizen in 1739. The parish register of Fiume has a De Franceschi household baptising children in the city in 1626.
lead: This was not found by looking for it. It came out of a sweep of the FamilySearch index for every record of the surname in Croatia with a date before 1700 — a query this archive had run before and never filtered this way. Three entries came back from a collection catalogued as «Croatia, Delnice Deanery Catholic Church Books», which sounds like the Gorski Kotar and is not: the film's own catalogue record names the creator as **«Rimokatolička crkva. Župa Rijeka»**, the parish of Rijeka. DGS 004679931.

All three were then read on the film, band by band, and all three are exactly what the index says they are. They are the earliest documented De Franceschi in the Kvarner by more than a century, and the company they keep is not the company of a weaver's family.

rows.lab: 6 September 1626 · folio 108
rows.q: Die sexta Septembris — P.br **Joannes Sardich** Baptizavit **Joannis Anthonij de Franceschi** filium nomine **Joannem Anth.m**, natum ex eius matre legitima nomine **Lucia**. Compatres autem fuerunt D. **Anthonius Jacobus Cursius** et D. **Margarita v.q.D. Anthonij Jachomin**.
rows.en: On the sixth day of September. Father Giovanni Sardić baptised the son of Giovanni Antonio de Franceschi, by name Giovanni Antonio, born of his lawful mother named Lucia. The godparents were Antonio Giacomo Cursio and Margarita, widow of the late Antonio Giacomino.
rows.why: The father is **Giovanni Antonio de Franceschi**; the mother is **Lucia**; the son takes the father's name entire. This is the household. Everything else on this page is the same two parents.

rows.lab: 19 April 1628 · folio 119 — and the godfather is the Captain of Fiume
rows.q: Die 19 Aprilis — Presbiter **Joannes Sardich** Baptizavit **Joannis Anthonij de Franceschi** filiam nomine **Joanna Victoriam**, natam ex eius matre legitima nomine **Lucia**. Compatres autem fuerunt Ill.mus D.nus **Stefanus, liber Baro a Rouuere, Invictissimi Ferdinandi Secundi Romanorum Imperatoris Consiliarius, et Camerarius ac Pincerna, ac Civitatis Fluminis Capitaneus**, et D. **Cassandra uxor D. Petri Mariae Monaldi**.
rows.en: On the 19th of April. Father Giovanni Sardić baptised the daughter of Giovanni Antonio de Franceschi, by name Giovanna Vittoria, born of his lawful mother named Lucia. The godparents were the most illustrious lord Stefano, free Baron della Rovere, Councillor, Chamberlain and Cupbearer to the most invincible Ferdinand II, Holy Roman Emperor, and Captain of the City of Fiume; and lady Cassandra, wife of Pietro Maria Monaldi.
rows.why: **The imperial captain of the city stood godfather to this child.** That is the highest office in Fiume, held by a baron of the Emperor's own household, and he is standing at the font for a De Franceschi baby. Whatever this family was in Fiume in 1628, it was not obscure.

rows.lab: 9 September 1632 · folio 143 — and this one was baptised by a bishop
rows.q: Die 9 7bris — Ill.mus et R.mus D.nus **Joannes Baptista Agatich, Episcopus Segniensis et Administrator Modrusiensis, S.S.C.M. Consiliarius**, Baptizavit **Joannis Anthonij de Franceschi** filiam nomine **Mariam**, natam ex eius matre legitima nomine **Lucia**, quae supradicta Maria fuit prius Catechizata a me, Plebano Fluminis. Compatres autem fuerunt D.nus **Joannes Josephus P[…], V. Con. Fluminis**, et D.na **Cassandra uxor D. Petri Mariae Monaldi**.
rows.en: On the 9th of September. The most illustrious and most reverend lord Giovanni Battista Agatić, Bishop of Senj and Administrator of Modruš, Councillor of His Sacred Caesarean Majesty, baptised the daughter of Giovanni Antonio de Franceschi, by name Maria, born of his lawful mother named Lucia — the said Maria having first been catechised by me, the parish priest of Fiume. The godparents were Giovanni Giuseppe P…, vice-consul of Fiume, and lady Cassandra, wife of Pietro Maria Monaldi.
rows.why: **The Bishop of Senj came and did it himself.** Ivan Krstitelj Agatić — Giovanni Battista Agatić — was bishop of Senj and Modruš and an imperial councillor; he is a figure in Croatian church history, not a passing curate. And Cassandra Monaldi is godmother for the second time in four years, which is what a family friend looks like in a register.

rows.lab: It moves the surname in Fiume back by 113 years
rows.text: Kobler's list — the one Carlo used and this archive publishes on **Carlo's Letter** — begins with Valentino, «come from Carnia, made a citizen in 1739». That is now the first *Carnian* Defranceschi of Fiume, not the first Defranceschi of Fiume. Somebody of the name was baptising children in the city in the reign of Ferdinand II, while the Thirty Years' War was on.

rows.lab: It is almost certainly not this family
rows.text: Every instinct this archive has built says so. The Carnian weavers come down after 1679; the Gologorica house is built in 1711; Carlo's own account has them in Istria «intorno al 1700». A household standing at the font with the imperial Captain of Fiume in 1628 is a different social world from a *tessitore contadino* of Mione. **De Franceschi is a patronymic and it formed independently everywhere the name Francesco was common.** The honest reading is: a Venetian or Friulian merchant family in Habsburg Fiume, a century before ours arrives, and no connection shown.

rows.lab: But it is the right kind of not-this-family
rows.text: It is worth saying why this matters anyway. This archive's own line ends at **Senj**, and the man who baptised Maria de Franceschi in 1632 was the Bishop of Senj. The line's own century in **Crikvenica and Klenovica** sits between the two cities. The surname was already in the Kvarner, at the top of it, three hundred years before Anton Rudolf was baptised at Klenovica house 22. Whoever they were, when the Gračišće stonecutter's son came down to this coast in the 1880s he was not bringing a new name to it.

rows.lab: What would settle it
rows.text: The Fiume registers themselves — the marriages, which would give Giovanni Antonio's origin and Lucia's surname, and the deaths. The civic records Kobler worked through, in the **Državni arhiv u Rijeci**. And Kobler's own «Memorie per la storia della liburnica città di Fiume», which this archive cites already and has never searched for a pre-1700 Franceschi. **None of that has been done.**

more.heading: And then the Omiš and Split records were read too — all four
more.lead: They were published on this page as **indexed, not read**. David asked for them to be opened. Three of the four have been, on the films, and they gave more than their index entries — including a correction to FamilySearch, an occurrence of the surname no index carries, and the oldest birth year this archive holds for anyone of the name.

rows.lab: Omiš, 12 January 1644 — and the index has the sex wrong
rows.q: L'Anno del Sig.re 1644 Adi 12 Genaro — … il Sig.r **Don Mateo Berkoveo d'Almissa**, Sac[erdote] Cur[a]to, ha battezato **il figlio nato li 9 instante di Cap.n Zuane de Franceschi et Sig.ra Elena coniugati**, al quale fu posto nome **Nicolò**, di questa Parochia. Compari furono Sig.r **Gierolimo Marinovich** et Sig.ra **Francesca de Franceschi**.
rows.en: In the year of the Lord 1644, the 12th of January. Don Matteo Berković of Almissa, priest and curate, baptised the son born on the 9th instant to Captain Zuane de Franceschi and lady Elena, husband and wife, on whom was placed the name Nicolò, of this parish. The godparents were Girolamo Marinović and lady Francesca de Franceschi.
rows.why:
**FamilySearch indexes this child as «Nicolaa De Franceschi, Female».** The register says «il figlio» and «al quale fu posto nome Nicolò». It is a boy. That is now corrected here.

And two things the index does not carry at all. The father is styled **Cap.n — Captain**. And the godmother is **Francesca de Franceschi**, a woman of the family, standing for her own kin: indexes transcribe parents and children, never godparents, so she exists in no index anywhere.

rows.lab: …and she is on the same page twice
rows.q: …et m[adonn]a Zuana giugali, al qual fu posto nome **Marco** di questa Parochia. Compari furono … **Cap.n Nicolò C[…]** et Sig.ra **Francesca de Franceschi**.
rows.en: …and lady Zuana, husband and wife, on whom was placed the name Marco, of this parish. The godparents were Captain Nicolò C… and lady Francesca de Franceschi.
rows.why: The entry directly above, in March 1644, for another family's son. **The same woman, the same page, a second godparent turn.** A De Franceschi standing at the font twice in one opening of the Omiš book is exactly the pattern this archive found at Svetvinčenat — the family that is always being asked. Neither appearance is in any index.

rows.lab: Omiš, 29 March 1645 — born about 1581, the oldest of all
rows.q: **Gioannes Maria de Franceschi** obijt **die 29 Martij, anno etatis suae 64**.
rows.en: Giovanni Maria de Franceschi died on the 29th of March, in the 64th year of his age.
rows.why:
One line in a column of deaths, with the year 1645 ruled off at the right. Sixty-four in 1645 means **born about 1581** — the earliest birth year for this surname anywhere in the Croatian record, and a full generation before the Fiume household above.

He is an exact contemporary of **Pietro Antonio detto Perini de Franceschi (1588–1661)**, the man at the head of the Omiš family's own twenty-generation chart. This archive is not going to make him Perini's brother on a shared surname and a shared decade. It will say that the chart's first generation, which has always rested on the family's own paper, now has a man of the name dying in the parish register beside it.

**One correction to the index:** FamilySearch dates this death 20 March. The register reads 29 — the same hand writes 28 four times in the lines below, and the glyph here carries the descender of a 9.

rows.lab: Split, 17 October 1700 — a child not expected to live
rows.q: Adì 17 Ottobre 1700 — **Antonio figlio di Egidio de Franceschi et di sua Consorte Maria**, al quale **fu data l'acqua in casa, in caso di necessità**, da me … Sac[erdote]; **et hoggi supplite le cerimonie** … **in Chiesa di S. Gio: Battista**, con licenza dell'Ill.mo … Compari furono Sig.r … Zuane Guido, con assistenza del …
rows.en: The 17th of October 1700. Antonio, son of Egidio de Franceschi and of his consort Maria, on whom the water was poured at home, in case of necessity, by me, priest; and today the ceremonies were supplied … in the church of St John the Baptist, by licence of the most illustrious … The godparents were … Zuane Guido, with the assistance of …
rows.why:
**«L'acqua in casa, in caso di necessità»** is the phrase for an emergency baptism: the child was thought to be dying and was christened where he lay. He lived, and the ceremonies were supplied in church afterwards — which is why there is a record at all, and why it is dated to the day of the supplying, not the day of the birth.

Split had never appeared on this site as a place of the name. It does now, with a household: **Egidio de Franceschi and Maria**, in the cathedral parish, in 1700. The last lines of the entry — the officiant and the second godparent — are still not read.

rows.lab: Split, 18 May 1716 — and he is a canon of Candia
rows.q:
**Adì 18 maggio 1716**
[Il M.to R.do Sig.r] **Can.co Don Nicolò de Franceschi** ⟨*Can.co di S. Vito di Candia*⟩ passò da questa alla miglior vita **d'anni 90 incirca**, munito de SS. Sacram.ti dal R.do Padre **Capucino**, capelano del Ospitale, et **fù sepolto nella Chiesa del Domo in Coro nella sepoltura delli Sig.ri Can.ci**.
rows.en: On the 18th of May 1716. The most reverend Canon Don Nicolò de Franceschi — *canon of St Vitus of Candia* — passed from this life to a better, aged about ninety, fortified with the holy sacraments by the reverend Capuchin father, chaplain of the hospital; and he was buried in the church of the Cathedral, in the choir, in the tomb of the canons.
rows.why:
The index called him «Nicolo De Franceschi, burial 18 May 1716, birth 1626». The register makes him somebody entirely different.

**He was a canon**, and he was buried where canons are buried: **in the choir of the cathedral of Split**, in the chapter's own vault. The cathedral of Split is Diocletian's mausoleum. He lies inside a Roman emperor's tomb.

**And then the words written in above his name, with a caret**: «**Can.co di S. Vito di Candia**» — *canon of St Vitus of Candia*. **Candia is Crete.**

Read it against the arithmetic. Ninety in 1716 means **born about 1626**, in Venetian Crete. **Candia fell to the Ottomans in September 1669** after the longest siege in European history; he would have been forty-three. A canon of a Cretan church, holding after 1669 a title to a chapter that no longer existed, ends his life in a Dalmatian cathedral and is buried with the canons of Split.

*(A note on the reading: the register writes «S. Vito». The great church of Candia was **San Tito** — St Titus — and a Split clerk setting down an exiled Cretan canonry could easily write Vito for Tito. This page gives what the register gives and says what it suspects.)*

rows.lab: And what that does to the Seget question
rows.why:
This archive carries a page arguing with Petar Puhmajer, who writes that the de Franceschi bought Seget from the Venier **in 1720**, having **fled from Crete after the Cretan War of 1669**, and that the Gologorica and Seget families are two branches of one. This site contests the second half of that and has always treated the first half — the Cretan flight — as **the family's own tradition**, recorded but not proved.

**It is no longer only tradition.** Here is a De Franceschi with a **Cretan canonry**, born about **1626**, dying in **Dalmatia** in **1716** — four years before the Seget purchase — and buried among the canons of Split.

It does not prove the Seget family's descent, and this page does not say it does. It proves something narrower and harder: **that men of this surname held office in Venetian Crete and ended up in Dalmatia after the fall of Candia.** The tradition now has a document standing next to it, and the place to test the rest is the **chapter records of Split** and the **Archivio del Duca di Candia** in Venice — where the family's nobility was already proved in 1488.

more.close: Four records, three read. Between them: one indexed sex corrected, one indexed date corrected, two godparent appearances that exist in no index, a **Captain** Zuane de Franceschi at Omiš in 1644, an emergency baptism at Split in 1700, and a man born about 1581 — the oldest date this archive has for anybody of the name in Croatia.

rovinj.heading: And Rovinj is older still — 27 May 1619
rovinj.lead: This page has called the Fiume household of 1626 the earliest thing in the archive. It is not. Seven years earlier, in a book of burial offerings at Rovinj, a clerk wrote three lines that are now the oldest dated appearance of this surname in Istria that this project holds.

rows.lab: «morì ser Piero di Franceschi da Pola»
rows.q:
**Adì 27 Mago 1619**
**morì ser Piero di Fran-**
**ceschi da Pola. Fu por-**
**tato il suo cad[avere] … off[erta] L 24**
rows.en: On the 27th of May 1619 died Ser Piero di Franceschi **of Pola**. His body was carried [here] … offering, 24 lire.
rows.why:
Three things in three lines.

**He is «ser».** Not *Dominus*, not plain — the Venetian courtesy for a man of standing below the patriciate: a merchant, a notary, a citizen.

**He is «da Pola».** He is not a Rovinj man. Rovinj's book has him because he died there or was brought there.

**«Fu portato il suo cadavere»** — *his body was carried*. Somebody paid to move him. And the offering is **24 lire**, where the entries above and below it on the same page run at 2, 6, 12 and 30. This is a book that records what each burial was worth to the church, and his was near the top of the page.

**Seven years before the Fiume baptisms, a hundred and forty-two years before the surname is first written at Gologorica, and eighty-one years before the family this site follows reaches Istria at all.**

rows.lab: And the second-oldest is a man of Vodnjan
rows.q: [27 Xbre 1728] e Sero. **Ob[ito] di Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano** — **L 6**
rows.en: [27 December 1728] and in the evening, the burial of Mattio de Franceschi **of Dignano** — 6 lire.
rows.why:
A hundred and nine years later, on the same film, the same book does it again — and **again the man is a stranger**. Piero is *of Pola*; Mattio is *of Dignano*, which is **Vodnjan**, twenty kilometres down the coast.

This archive's inventory of regions lists **Vodnjan** among the *unplaced* — a town where the surname occurs and nothing joins it to anything. It now has a named man and a date. So does Pola, seventy years before the run of Pula baptisms this project already reads from 1659.

**The two oldest De Franceschi on the Rovinj film are not Rovinj people at all.** That is worth saying plainly, because a record found in a town's register is normally taken to mean a family of that town, and here it means the opposite: **a register of burial offerings catches whoever dies inside the parish**, including the traveller and the man carried in from somewhere else.

rows.lab: What else the Rovinj film holds
rows.why:
Sixteen records in all, and the shape of them is a **household at Rovinj across three generations** that this archive has never written up:

· **Giacomo** → **Vittorio de Franceschi**, who marries **Domenica Moscarda**, daughter of Nicolò
· **Vittorio** and **Franca** → **Piero Anto**, baptised **1736**
· **Mattio de Franceschi** and **Elisabetta** → **Martino**, baptised **1722**
· **Franco de Franceschi** and **Menegha**
· **Pietro Defranceschi** and **Elisabetta Dalino**, daughter of Pietro — about 1793
· **Sinforosa De Franceschi**, daughter of Giovanni, and **Maria**, who marries Gio Batta Volsi — about 1801
· **Bona Defranceschi**, daughter of **Dominicus Defranceschi and Oliva Dorligurro**, marrying Antonius Medelin — 1843
· burials: **Petrus, son of Michael**, born 1790, died 12 June 1864; **Petrus, son of Joseph**, born 1765, died 19 January 1829; and **Julius, son of Carlo**, born 1853, dead **13 February 1854** at a few months old

**And one that is ours.** On the same film: **Carlo De Franceschi, son of «Giuseppe da Gologorizza» and «Lambertina Pesle», marrying Maria Michelcich, daughter of Luca and Maria.** That is the historian of Istria — his parents named exactly as the Gologorica household books name them — with his marriage indexed on a Rovinj film. **The image has now been opened — see below.** It is the next thing to read on this reel.

rows.lab: 1 March 1852 — Carlo De Franceschi is married at his own bedside
rows.q:
**31** · Addì 1 Marzo **1852** · **Rovigno**

«**Il Signor Carlo De Franceschi q.m Giuseppe e della Sig.ra Lambertina Pesle di Mattia,
da Gologorizza di Pisino, Assessore presso quest'I. R. Corte di Giustizia**,
**celibe, d'anni 40**, contrasse matrimonio **per verba de praesenti**
colla **Sig.ra Maria Michelcich di Luca e di Maria, celibe, d'anni 26**;
**dispensati dalle trine pubblicazioni dall'Imp. Reg. Capitanato Distrettuale,
urgente necessitate, colla nota del primo Marzo c. № 898**; confessati e communicati,
interrogati furono del loro mutuo libero consenso …
**Domenico Quarantotto, Coop.** … **al letto dello Sposo, per essere gravemente
ammalato**, nella casa al № … alla presenza delli Signori **Zaccaria Maver,
Procuratore di Stato sostituto**, e **D.r Barzan, Medico**, testimonj.»
rows.why:
This is the most-cited De Franceschi in Istria — the historian, the deputy, the man whose *L'Istria* this archive spends a whole page arguing with — and **his own wedding has never been read here until tonight**.

It is not the wedding anyone would have imagined. **He was married lying down.** The priest came to the house and performed it «**al letto dello Sposo, per essere gravemente ammalato**» — at the bridegroom's bed, because he was gravely ill. The three readings of the banns were **dispensed by the Imperial-Royal District Captaincy that same day**, on urgent necessity, by a note numbered **898**: the machinery of the Austrian state turned around in hours because a man was thought to be dying.

The witnesses are not family. They are **Zaccaria Maver, deputy State Prosecutor**, and **Dr Barzan, the physician** — the law and the medicine, which is exactly who is in the room when a marriage has to be got through before it is too late.

And the entry gives in one line what this archive had been assembling from elsewhere: **father Giuseppe, mother Lambertina Pesle di Mattia, of Gologorizza di Pisino** — Gologorica, under Pazin — and his office at the time, **Assessore at the Imperial-Royal Court of Justice** at Rovinj. *(doc)*

**He did not die.** He lived another forty-one years, to 1893.

One discrepancy, stated: the register calls him **d'anni 40**. Carlo was born **16 October 1809**, which makes him **forty-two** that March. Ages in these books are what somebody said in the room, and in this room the man being asked was too ill to stand. *(doc for the entry; the age is the register's, and it is wrong)*

rows.lab: And then, two years later, a small coffin
rows.text:
On the same Rovinj film, logged by this archive before the marriage was ever read: a burial of **«Julius, son of Carlo», born 1853, dead 13 February 1854** at a few months old.

Set beside the entry above, that is very likely **the first child of this marriage** — conceived within a year of a wedding held at a sickbed, and buried before his first birthday. *(doc for both records; that they are one family is inf, and rests on the name, the place and the dates)*

vodnjan.heading: Vodnjan: a question, a wrong answer, and then the register
vodnjan.lead: David asked whether this archive was seeing records from Vodnjan. The first answer given was **no, and the seventy-eight records credited to the town are really Vižinada's**. That answer was wrong, it stood on this page for about an hour, and the register itself overturned it.

rows.lab: How the wrong answer was reached, and why it failed
rows.text:
The check looked sound. The eighteen-town sweep counted by **place-name**; the later sweep resolved records to **the parish reel they sit on** and produced ninety-three parishes with no Vodnjan among them. Following the image arks gave **DGS 005497893**, and asking the catalogue who made that film returned **«Rimokatolička crkva. Župa Vižinada»**. Case apparently closed.

**The catalogue answers by film, and a film can carry more than one parish.** Reel 005497893 holds two items:

· **Vižinada** — *Umrli 1754–1831*, the deaths
· **Vodnjan** — *Rođeni 1815–1866*, the baptisms

A search by film number returns the first creator on the reel. **The method was right and the question put to it was wrong**, and this archive published the result inside twenty minutes without opening a single image. The regions row has been restored.

rows.lab: The registers, found
rows.text:
FamilySearch catalogue item **koha:963267**: «*Metrical books (births, marriages, deaths) for the Roman Catholic congregation at **Dignano, Küstenland, Austria; later Vodnjan, Croatia**. Text in Italian.*»

· **DGS 005497893** — **baptisms 1815–1866**
· **DGS 005497894** — baptisms 1867–1878 · **marriages 1815–1884** · deaths 1815–1833
· **DGS 005497895** — **deaths 1834–1893**

**Seventy-eight years of baptisms, seventy of marriages, seventy-eight of deaths**, and until today this project did not know they existed.

rows.lab: «LIBER BAPTIZATORUM IN ECCLESIA S. BLASII DIGNANI»
rows.q:
**149** · 4 Decembre [1816] · **№ domus 376**
**D. Stefano De Franceschi (de Parocho licentia)**
**Domenica Maria De Franceschi**, nata li 1.mo Decembre
Catholica · Femina · Legitima
**Pater: Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe, agricoltore**
**Mater: Maria Malusà q.m Matteo di Antonio**
Patrini: Pietro Ved… di Raffael × Maria Lu…anza di Franc…
**Conditio: Civile**
rows.why:
The book is headed for the **church of St Blaise of Dignano** — the great basilica of Vodnjan — and the first De Franceschi entry gives more in one ruled line than most parishes give in a paragraph.

**A house number: 376.** **A grandfather: Pietro is «di Giuseppe».** **A mother with three generations of her own: Maria Malusà, daughter of the late Matteo, son of Antonio.** And a status: **civile**.

**And look who is holding the child.** The baptising column reads «**D. Stefano De Franceschi, de Parocho licentia**» — Don Stefano De Franceschi, by licence of the parish priest. **A priest of this surname was serving at Vodnjan in 1816**, and he is not baptising only his own kin: on the facing page, on 1 January 1817, he baptises a Mescheni child whose mother is **Michiela De Franceschi di Giovanni**.

**A priest of the name, and at least five lay households of it, in one small Istrian town.** This archive has never had that anywhere except Gologorica.

rows.lab: The five households, now anchored
rows.text:
Indexed, and now known to be **Vodnjan** rather than nowhere:

· **Pietro × Maria Malusà** — Domenica Maria 1816, Domenica Michiela Giovanna 1818, Teresa Domenica 1820, Stefano Matteo 1822, Cristoforo 1824
· **Pietro × Maddalena Francin** — Maria Martina 1822, Pasqua 1824, Giovanni 1827, Lucia 1828
· **Domenico × Zacchera Cerlon** — Pietro 1817, Pietro 1819, Franco 1821, Domenica 1822, Pasqua 1825, Pietro 1828, Domenica 1830, Maria 1833; then × **Pasqua Gorlato** — Maria 1839; then × **Maria Oliva Dorliguzzo** — Pietro 1837, Bonetta 1841, Arveneria 1844
· **Stefano × Bonetta Vellico** — Domenico Giovanni Anto 1819, Martina 1824, Maria 1829
· **Gio Maria × Lucia Bonassin** — Veniera 1822, Lucia 1826, Giovanni 1829, Stefano 1831

**Domenico baptises three sons called Pietro in eleven years** and buries two wives. **The marriage register, 1815–1884, is on film 005497894 and would name every one of these wives' fathers.** It has not been opened.

rows.lab: And the death on that reel is somebody else's
rows.q: **7 [Augusti 1819] · № domus 32 · Mathaeus De Franceschi fil[ius] Antonii**
rows.why:
The one death record among these is not Vodnjan's at all. Its page is headed «**LIBER DEFUNCTORUM — Castellier**» — **Kaštelir**, a chapelry under **Vižinada**, in the deaths section at the front of the same reel.

So the film really does carry De Franceschi in **two parishes forty kilometres apart**, and that is exactly why the wrong answer looked right. **Mathaeus De Franceschi, son of Anton, of house 32 at Kaštelir, born about 1750, died 7 August 1819** — and he belongs on the Vižinada side of the reel, not the Vodnjan one.

rows.lab: Vodnjan and Rovinj, joined at both ends of a century
rows.text:
Two records now tie the two towns together.

**1728** — in the Rovinj book of burial offerings: «**Ob.to di Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano — L 6**». A man of Vodnjan, dead in Rovinj.

**1840s** — on the Rovinj film: **Bona Defranceschi, daughter of Dominicus Defranceschi and Oliva Dorligurro**, marrying **Antonius Medelin**. That is the third household above — Domenico's third marriage — sending a daughter to Rovinj.

**Both of these places sat in this archive's inventory as «unplaced».** They are not unconnected; they are connected to each other, a hundred and twenty years apart, and nobody had put the two rows side by side.

rows.lab: «LIBER COPULATORUM IN ECCLESIA S. BLASII ADIGNANI»
rows.text:
The marriage book is on **DGS 005497894**, and **FamilySearch has never indexed it**. Two hundred and eighty-six marriage-query arks were resolved against that film and **not one** of them landed on it. Every marriage in this section has therefore been read off the page by eye, opening after opening.

The volume's cover is at **image 170**; the first entry, *Annus 1815*, at **image 172**; the next volume begins at **image 266**. Roughly ninety-four openings, **1815 to 1884**. The folio numbers are stamped in the corner and run odd on the right — 178 recto is folio 11, 179 recto folio 13 — so the reading order can be checked against the book itself rather than against the film.

What follows is images **172–182**: *doc* on every line, because every line was photographed and read.

rows.lab: 30 March 1818 — the marriage this archive came for
rows.q:
**15** · 30 Marzo [1818] · **№ domus 312**

**Sponsus** — **Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio. Maria**,
vedovo della q.m **Veniera Franzin q.m Domenico**
Cattolico · **d'Anni 42** · **Vedovo**

**Sponsa** — **Lorenza Tesser q.m Ambrogio**,
vedova del q.m **Andrea Manzin fu altro Andrea**
Cattolica · **d'Anni 40** · **Vedova**

**Testes** — + Gio. Batta d'Ambra, **fabbro**
+ Antonio Bellicaglia di Giovanni, **muratore**
rows.why:
A whole generation arrives in six lines. **Pietro is forty-two**, so born about **1776** — and his father **Gio. Maria De Franceschi is already dead**, which carries the family in Vodnjan back into the middle of the eighteenth century, well behind the register's own first page. He is a **widower**: there was a first wife, **Veniera Franzin**, daughter of a Domenico Franzin, and she died before March 1818. He marries another widow, **Lorenza Tesser**, whose first husband was Andrea Manzin.

This is **not** the Pietro of the baptism above. That one is «**Pietro De Franceschi *di* Giuseppe**» — *di*, father living. This one is «*q.m* Gio. Maria» — father dead. **Two men of the same name in one small town at the same moment**, and the register keeps them apart by naming the father every single time. *(doc)*

One caution, marked plainly: the baptism register of 1816 records **Gio Maria De Franceschi** as a living household head. If Pietro's father Gio. Maria was dead by 1818, then the Gio Maria fathering children in the 1820s is **a second man of the name** — most likely a grandson. That is an inference and it is not yet proved. *(inf)*

rows.lab: Two brothers, and both of them sign with a cross
rows.text:
Twice in 1818 a De Franceschi stands as witness, and both times the clerk writes a **cross** before the name — the mark of a man who cannot write his own.

**30 March 1818**, entry 14, house 391, at the wedding of Lorenzo Bilucaglia and Domenica Giacometti:
«**+ Cristoforo De Franceschi di Giuseppe** — *Tessitore*» — **a weaver**.

**14 September 1818**, entry 25, house 457, at the wedding of Domenico Coffetti and Maria Zoghil da Gimino:
«**+ Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe** — *Agricoltore*» — the father of the child baptised in December 1816.

**Cristoforo and Pietro, both «di Giuseppe».** Same father, alive, named the same way in the same hand within six months: they are **brothers**. *(inf, and a strong one)*

And a tension worth stating rather than smoothing over. The baptism of December 1816 records the household's *Conditio* as **civile**. The marriage register calls Pietro **agricoltore** and shows him **unable to sign**. Those are the two columns of two different books and they may simply be asking different questions — but this archive is not going to quietly publish the flattering one. *(doc for both readings; the reconciliation is unresolved)*

rows.lab: Don Stefano De Franceschi, placed — and then given a father
rows.q:
**15** · 7 Giugno [1819] · **№ domus 718**

**Sponsus** — Antonio, figlio di Domenico Belci q.m Andrea
e Domenica Giachin q.m Domenico

**Sponsa** — Natalia, figlia del q.m Stefano Codalovich q.m Ant.o
e di Vita Tromba q.m Cristoforo · **d'Anni 20**

**Testes** — **Don Stefano De Franceschi — *Sacerdote***
Martino Fioranti fu Giò. — *Artista*

*Joannes Tromba Sac. Theol. Doct. Parochus Capitulique Praepositus*
rows.why:
In the baptism of 4 December 1816 he appears as «**D. Stefano De Franceschi (de Parocho licentia)**» — he baptised the child **by the parish priest's leave**, which told us he was a priest but not which one, or whose. Here he is again, thirty months later, **signing as a witness in his own right and styled simply *Sacerdote***.

And the foot of the page names the man who gave him that leave: **Giovanni Tromba, Doctor of Sacred Theology, parish priest and Provost of the Chapter**. So Don Stefano was **not** the parish priest of Vodnjan. He was **a priest of the town**, one of the chapter's clergy, free to be asked for at a family baptism and to stand up at a neighbour's wedding.

He is also, so far, the only literate De Franceschi in Vodnjan — the only one whose name is written without a cross in front of it. *(doc)*

And then, on **17 August 1820**, the clerk writes him out in full:

> **«D.n Stefano De Franceschi *di Giuseppe* — Sacerdote»**

*Di Giuseppe.* The same patronymic, in the same hand, in the same book, as **«+ Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe, agricoltore»** and **«+ Cristoforo De Franceschi di Giuseppe, tessitore»**.

**They are brothers.** A priest, a ploughman and a weaver, sons of one Giuseppe De Franceschi of Vodnjan — and the two who worked with their hands could not sign their names while the third was writing in the register. *(doc for all three readings; the brotherhood is inf, and about as firm as an inference gets)*

rows.lab: Domenica De Franceschi, dead before the book begins
rows.q:
**21** · 19 Novembre [1817] · **№ domus 145**

**Sponsus** — Giuseppe, figlio di Fran.co Manzin q.m Giuseppe
e di Cattarina Manzin q.m Andrea · **d'Anni 25**

**Sponsa** — Giovanna, figlia di Tommaso Mivinurro q.m Gio.
e della **fu Dom.ca De Franceschi** · **d'Anni 40**
rows.why:
The bride is **forty** in 1817, so born about **1777**, and her mother — **Domenica De Franceschi** — was already dead when the entry was written.

Run it backwards. A woman whose daughter was born in 1777 was herself born somewhere around **1750**. She was baptised, married and buried in a Vodnjan whose registers, on this film, **do not start until 1815**. She is the reach of this book backwards past its own first page: **proof of De Franceschi in Vodnjan by the middle of the eighteenth century**, from a record written sixty years later. *(doc for the entry; the arithmetic is inf)*

She also sits within a lifetime of «**Ob.to di Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano**», buried at Rovinj on 27 December **1728** — until today the only evidence this archive had that the name was in the town at all.

rows.lab: Nineteen times a witness, and the company he kept
rows.text:
Don Stefano turns up again and again in the years the register has so far given up, and **who he stands beside is the point**.

· **7 June 1819**, house 718 — with *Martino Fioranti fu Giò., artista*
· **20 August 1819**, house 246 — with the **Reverendissimo Signor D. Michiel Benedetto, Canonico Coffetti**
· **17 August 1820**, house 161 — with **D.r Antonio De Marchi q.m Antonio, sacerdote**, and here he is «**di Giuseppe**»
· **13 November 1820**, house 588 — with **D. Antonio De Marchi** again
· **3 July 1822**, house 200 — with *Giacomo De Marchi q.m Antonio, agricoltore*
· **28 October 1824**, house 208 — with **Canon Michiel Benedetto** again
· **16 February 1828**, house 464 — with **D. Antonio De Marchi**, the two entered together as *Sacerdoti*
· **23 September 1828**, house 73 — with **D. Giacomo Tosoni**, *Sacerdote*
· **25 November 1828**, house 344 — with *Egidio De Maria fu Nicolò, possidente*
· **25 November 1828**, house 329 — **the same day, the next couple**, with Giacomo De Marchi, *nunzolo*

He is never the officiant and never the parroco: **Giovanni Tromba, Doctor of Sacred Theology**, signs the foot of every page as *Parochus Capitulique Praepositus*. Don Stefano is a **priest of the chapter**, called on by families and standing at the altar rail beside canons.

His brothers, in the same years, are being written into the same book with a **cross** in front of their names. *(doc)*

· **23 May 1829**, house 281 — in the **church of San Martino**, with **Ferdinando Verbits, *Maestro delle Scuole Elementari***
· **31 August 1829**, house 51 — with Giacomo De Marchi, *nunzolo*
· **19 December 1829**, house 294 — with **D. Giacomo Tosoni**, on a dispensation from the three readings of the banns granted by the **Imperial-Royal Circle Captaincy**
· **22 December 1829**, house 516 — with **Canon Tommaso Belli**, the two entered as *Ecclesiastici*

· **8 June 1830**, house 61 — with Giacomo De Marchi, on a fourth-degree dispensation
· **24 November 1830**, house 380 — with Giovanni Prencis q.m Lorenzo

· **3 August 1831**, house 293 — with **Canon Cristoforo Paolino Pagano**
· **17 January 1832**, house 376 — with **D. Antonio De Marchi, sagrestano**

· **16 November 1832**, house 77 — with **D.n Filippo De Marchi**, *sacerdote*

**Nineteen times in thirteen years.** Twice on the same afternoon of 25 November 1828. Never once as the officiant — that is always **Giovanni Tromba**, the parroco.

And look at who is standing beside him: canons, priests, a doctor of theology, and in May 1829 the town's **elementary schoolmaster**. Don Stefano moves in the small literate world of Vodnjan while his two brothers, in the same volume, are marked with a cross because they cannot write.

rows.lab: A second sister, alive in 1819
rows.q:
**19** · 30 Giugno [1819] · **№ domus 13**

**Sponsus** — Dom.co De Rocchi, figlio del fu Dom.co De Rocchi fu Veniere
e di Antonia Forlani q.m Ant.o, **vedovo della fu Vita Manzin**

**Sponsa** — **Martina Antonia**, figlia del fu Damiano Storcovich
e **della vivente Antonia Maria De Franceschi** giugali
Cattolica · **d'Anni 40**
rows.why:
*Della vivente* — **still living**. Where Domenica De Franceschi was «la fu» in 1817, **Antonia Maria** is alive in June 1819, widow of Damiano Storcovich, with a daughter of forty.

So the register holds **two De Franceschi women of the generation born around 1750**, both married out of the name — one dead, one alive — whose daughters were born about **1777** and **1779**. They are almost certainly sisters, and they belong to a Vodnjan household that no register on this film reaches. *(doc for both entries; the sisterhood is inf)*

That matters for the shape of the thing. The five lay households of the baptism book are not the beginning of the De Franceschi in Vodnjan. They are **the middle of it**.

rows.lab: 9 June 1821 — the household gets a grandfather, and a guess is retired
rows.q:
**9** · 9 Giugno [1821] · **№ domus 356**

**Sponsus et Genitores** — **Gio: Maria De Franceschi**,
**figlio di Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria**
**e della fu Veniera Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel**,
giugali, **Agricoltori** · Cattolico · **d'Anni 22** · Celibe

**Sponsa et Genitores** — **Lucia**, figlia di **Giovanni Bonassin q.m Giuseppe**
e della **fu Lucia Davanzo q.m Leonardo**, giugali, Agricoltori
Cattolica · **d'Anni 27** · Celibe

**Testes** — Pietro Ghechig q.m Venier, *Agricoltore*
Giacomo De Marchi q.m Antonio, *Agricoltore*
rows.why:
In 1821 the register changes its ruling. The columns become **«Sponsus *et Genitores*»** — the parents of both parties, in every entry, by name. From this page on the book gives pedigree instead of hints.

And the first thing it gives is the whole line.

**Gio: Maria De Franceschi**, twenty-two, is the son of **Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria** — the very man who remarried in this book on **30 March 1818** — and of **Veniera Francin**, Pietro's first wife, the one already dead when he did. The bride is **Lucia Bonassin**, and «**Gio Maria De Franceschi × Lucia Bonassin**» is one of the households this archive reconstructed out of the baptism register months ago, with four children between 1822 and 1831.

So the household now stands four deep, off a single page:

· **Gio. Maria De Franceschi** — dead before 1818
· **Pietro**, born about **1776**; married Veniera Francin, then Lorenza Tesser in 1818
· **Gio: Maria**, born about **1799**; married **Lucia Bonassin** on 9 June 1821
· and their four children, 1822–1831

**And it retires this morning's guess.** When Pietro's father turned out to be dead by 1818, this page said the Gio Maria fathering children in the 1820s had to be a **second man of the name, most likely a grandson**, and marked it *inf* because it was not proved. It is proved now, and he is exactly that: **grandson, named for the grandfather**. *(doc)*

rows.lab: A third woman of the name, and a wedding full of nobles
rows.q:
**20** · 14 Novembre [1821] · **№ domus 54**

**Sponsus** — **Lorenzo**, figlio di Dom.co Michiele Mainuzzo q.m Andrea
e di Bonetta Forlani di Lorenzo, giugali · **d'Anni 21**

**Sponsa** — **Maria**, figlia di **Alvise Birattan q.m Saba**
e di **Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro**, giugali · **d'Anni 21**

**Testes** — Sig. **Giannandrea Dalla Zonca q.m Benedetto, Nobile**
Sig. **Guglielmo Conte Lombardo di Felice, da Pola, Nobile**

*Dispensa dal quarto grado di consanguinità, sub № 23*
rows.why:
**Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro** — a third woman of the name married out of it, after Domenica and Antonia Maria. Her daughter is twenty-one, so born about **1800**; Lucia herself married by 1799 and her father **Pietro** was dead by 1821. He cannot be the Pietro who remarried in 1818, who was only forty-two — so this is **an older Pietro again**, and another branch the baptism register never reaches.

And look who signs. Not a ploughman and a weaver but **Giannandrea Dalla Zonca**, of the family that gave Vodnjan its best-known nineteenth-century writer, and **Count Guglielmo Lombardo of Pola** — two nobles standing up at the wedding of a granddaughter of a De Franceschi. The couple also needed a **dispensation in the fourth degree of consanguinity**, which is the register quietly telling us these families had married each other before. *(doc)*

rows.lab: One to be careful about
rows.text:
On 13 February 1822 the register marries a **Chiara, figlia di Gio Batta Malusà q.m Gio e Maddalena *Franceschich* q.m Gio, giugali di Pinguente**.

**Franceschich is not Franceschi.** It is a Slavic patronymic out of **Buzet**, and it will match a loose search every time. This archive is reading these pages precisely so that names like that one are ruled out by eye rather than swept in by a query. *(doc — and recorded as a miss, deliberately)*

rows.lab: «da Dignano» — the name written down from outside the town
rows.q:
**4** · 30 Gennaro [1824] · **№ domus 409**

**Testes** — Matteo Tromba q.m Gio. **da Sissano**, *Agricoltore*
**Pietro De Franceschi di Gio., da Dignano — Tessitore**

*D.n Giannantonio Bozorich, Cooperatore di Sissano, li sposò in Sissano*
rows.why:
The couple were married not at St Blaise but at **Šišan (Sissano)**, ten kilometres south, by that village's own curate — and because the clerk is writing about strangers he says where each man is **from**. So the witness is set down as «**Pietro De Franceschi *di Gio.*, da Dignano, Tessitore**».

Two things come out of that line.

**A man this archive did not have.** Not Pietro *di Giuseppe* the ploughman, not Pietro *q.m Gio. Maria* who remarried in 1818 aged forty-two — a **Pietro son of a Giovanni, and a weaver**. The clerk writes «di Giuseppe» in full elsewhere in the same book, so the abbreviation is his own and it means Giovanni. *(doc; that he is a fourth distinct Pietro is inf, and the possibility of a slip is left standing)*

**And it is the same formula as 1728.** «Ob.to di **Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano**», in the Rovinj book of burial offerings. A man of this family is called *of Vodnjan* only when he is written about somewhere else. Ninety-six years apart, in two different parishes' books, the same phrase does the same work.

rows.lab: Lucia's second daughter
rows.q:
**21** · 14 Giugno [1824] · **№ domus 278**

**Sponsa** — **Bianca**, figlia di **Alvise Birattan q.m Saba**
e di **Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro**, giugali
Cattolica · **d'Anni 20** · Celibe

**Testes** — D. Michiel Benedetto, Can.co Coffetti, *Ecclesiastico*
Giacomo De Marchi q.m Antonio, *Agricoltore*
rows.why:
The same couple as November 1821 — **Alvise Birattan and Lucia De Franceschi** — marrying off a second daughter three years later. Maria was twenty-one in 1821, Bianca is twenty in 1824, so the two girls were born about **1800** and **1804** and their mother was married by 1799.

One household, two entries, and between them they fix Lucia's generation without a baptismal record existing for any of them. *(doc)*

rows.lab: A second line, and it goes back to a Domenico
rows.q:
**34** · 19 Novembre [1823] · **№ domus 684**

**Sponsa** — **Bonetta**, figlia **del fu Pietro De Franceschi q.m Dom.co**
e **Domenica Manzin q.m Dom.co**, giugali
Cattolica · **d'Anni 23** · Celibe

— and three months later —

**6** · 28 Febbraio [1824] · **№ domus 764**

**Testes** — Matteo Rotta di Gio.
**Pietro De Franceschi q.m Pietro** — *agricoltori*
rows.why:
Two entries, ninety days apart, and between them a **second male line** that has nothing to do with Giuseppe's three sons or with Gio: Maria's household.

**Pietro De Franceschi q.m Domenico**, married to **Domenica Manzin q.m Domenico**, dead by November 1823. His daughter **Bonetta** is twenty-three, so born about **1800**. And in February a **Pietro De Franceschi *q.m Pietro*** signs as a witness — a man whose father Pietro is dead, in the same parish, in the same season. He is almost certainly **Bonetta's brother**. *(doc for both entries; the brother-and-sister reading is inf)*

So the line stands:

· **Domenico De Franceschi** — dead before his son was written down this way
· **Pietro q.m Domenico** × Domenica Manzin — dead by 1823
· **Bonetta**, born about 1800, married 1823 · **Pietro q.m Pietro**, ploughman, 1824

That is a **Domenico at the head of it**, and Domenico is the given name that runs through three of the eight households the baptism register produced. Whether this Pietro is also the «q.m Pietro» who fathered **Lucia** — married out by 1799 — the register has not yet said, and this archive will not decide it on the strength of a shared forename. *(open)*

rows.lab: A third daughter — and a name this archive got wrong
rows.q:
**1** · 15 Gennaro **1825** · **№ domus 667**

**Sponsus** — **Gio. Maria**, figlio delli fu giugali Andrea Fioranti q.m Antonio
e Veniera Bonassin fu Gio. Ma. q.m Francesco · **d'Anni 32**

**Sponsa** — **Lucia**, figlia di **Alvise Birattan q.m Saba**
e di **Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro** · **d'Anni 28**

**Testes** — D.r Giacomo Tosoni, *Sacerdote* · Giacomo De Marchi q.m Ant.o
rows.why:
**A third daughter of the same couple**, and with her the household is complete on the page:

· **Lucia**, 28 in January 1825 — born about **1797**
· **Maria**, 21 in November 1821 — born about **1800**
· **Bianca**, 20 in June 1824 — born about **1804**

So **Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro was married by about 1796**, and her father Pietro was dead well before 1821. Three weddings out of one house, and not one of these women appears in any index anywhere.

**And a correction, in the place where the mistake was made.** Earlier today this page called the husband «**Alvise Bortolan** q.m Saba». That was a misreading of the hand. This third entry writes it clearly, and the two earlier ones say the same thing when you go back and look: the name is «**Alvise Birattan q.m Saba**». *Bortolan* was this archive's word, not the register's, and it has been changed above.

rows.lab: Pietro had a brother, and the first line widens
rows.q:
**6** · 25 Gennaro **1826** · **№ domus 224**

**Sponsa** — **Michiela**, figlia di **Cristoforo De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria**
e di **Maria Luigia Manzin q.m Domenico**, giugali
Cattolica · **d'Anni 26** · Celibe

**Testes** — Giacomo De Marchi fu Ant.o · Manzin Manzin fu Dom.co, *Agricoltori*
rows.why:
**«q.m Gio: Maria»** — the same dead father as the Pietro who remarried in March 1818 at forty-two. So **Cristoforo is Pietro's brother**, and the eldest line in Vodnjan now has two sons in it instead of one:

· **Gio. Maria De Franceschi**, dead before 1818
· **Pietro**, born about 1776 → his son **Gio: Maria**, married 1821
· **Cristoforo** × **Maria Luigia Manzin q.m Domenico** → his daughter **Michiela**, born about 1800, married 1826

**And here is the trap this parish sets.** There are now **two men called Cristoforo De Franceschi alive in Vodnjan at the same time**: this one, *q.m Gio: Maria*, and the **weaver**, *di Giuseppe*, who signed with a cross in 1818. They are not the same man and they are not in the same family. The register keeps them apart by the father's name and by nothing else — which is exactly why these pages have to be read rather than searched. *(doc)*

rows.lab: Antonio, son of Vittorio, at a wedding in Svetvinčenat
rows.q:
**29** · 10 Luglio **1826** · **№ domus 18**

**Testes** — **Ant.o De Franceschi fu Vittorio**
Martino Suspich q.m Martino — *Agricoltori*

*D.n Alessandro Fonsa, arciprete, li congiunse in **Sanvicenti***
rows.why:
Another wedding held outside the parish — this time at **Savičenta, which is Svetvinčenat** — and again the outside venue makes the clerk name people properly.

**«Antonio De Franceschi fu Vittorio».** *Vittorio* is not a Vodnjan name in anything read so far. It is a **Rovinj** name: the household this archive pulled off the Rovinj film runs **Giacomo → Vittorio, with Domenica Moscarda → Piero Anto, 1736**.

And **Svetvinčenat** is the parish where this archive has been reading a quite separate cluster — Mattia 1669, Mattio 1674, Piero 1707, and the nineteen openings of baptisms finished earlier this week.

So one line of a Vodnjan marriage register touches **both** of the other southern Istrian places at once: a man carrying a Rovinj given-name in his patronymic, standing up at a wedding in Svetvinčenat. This archive is **not** going to claim the three clusters are one family on that. It is recording that the register put them in the same room. *(doc for the entry; any connection is open, and unproved)*

rows.lab: Veniera, and now they are three
rows.q:
**4** · 7 Febraro **1828** · **№ domus 366**

**Sponsa** — **Michiela Damiana**, figlia del fu Domenico Pastrovicchio q.m Matteo
e **della vivente Veniera De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria**, giugali
Cattolica · **d'Anni 20** · Celibe

**Testes** — **Cristoforo De Franceschi fu Gio: M.a — *Agricoltore***
Giovanni Fabro fu Matteo — *Sarto*
rows.why:
One entry, and the eldest Vodnjan line acquires a **sister and a third child**.

**Veniera De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria** is *della vivente* — alive in February 1828 — widow of Domenico Pastrovicchio. Her daughter is twenty, born about **1808**. And standing as witness at that daughter's wedding is **Cristoforo De Franceschi fu Gio: Maria**: her own brother, at his niece's marriage.

So the children of **Gio. Maria De Franceschi**, dead before 1818, now number three:

· **Pietro**, born about 1776 — remarried 1818, father of the Gio: Maria who married in 1821
· **Cristoforo** — *agricoltore*, married to Maria Luigia Manzin, father of the Michiela who married in 1826
· **Veniera** — married Domenico Pastrovicchio, widowed, alive in 1828

The register found all three by naming their dead father the same way, three times, across ten years. **Not one of them has a baptism on any film this archive can reach.** *(doc)*

A note on the given name: Pietro's first wife was **Veniera Francin**, and his sister was **Veniera**. In a town this size the same handful of names does all the work, which is exactly why the patronymic is the only thing here worth trusting.

rows.lab: The weaver again, this time at home
rows.q:
**26** · 23 Settembre **1828** · **№ domus 313**

**Testes** — Giacomo De Marchi fu Ant.o, *Nunzolo*
**Pietro De Franceschi di Gio. — Tessitore**
D.r Antonio De Marchi, *Sacerdote*
rows.why:
The same man as the wedding at Šišan four years earlier — «**Pietro De Franceschi di Gio., Tessitore**» — and this time in Vodnjan itself, so the clerk drops the «da Dignano».

That settles something small but useful: he was **not a visitor**. He lived there, and the 1824 entry named his town only because the wedding did not. *(doc)*

rows.lab: The weaver, named in full
rows.q:
**44** · 25 Novembre **1828** · **№ domus 344**

**Testes** — Giovanni Prenis di Lorenzo, *Falegname*
**Cristoforo De Franceschi di Giuseppe — Tessitore**
rows.why:
Ten years after he signed with a cross in March 1818, **Cristoforo De Franceschi *di Giuseppe*, weaver**, is a witness again — and this time the clerk writes the patronymic out, which is what makes him safely separable from the **other** Cristoforo, *fu Gio: Maria*, the ploughman who witnessed his niece's wedding earlier the same year.

Two men, one name, one town, ten months apart in the same volume. **Only the father's name tells them apart**, and only because this clerk happened to write it. *(doc)*

rows.lab: The near-miss that matters most
rows.q:
**42** · 25 Novembre **1828** · **№ domus 344**

**Sponsus** — **Giuseppe**, figlio del fu **Pietro Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel**
e di Maria Vellico q.m Giuseppe, giugali · **d'Anni 19**
rows.why:
At a glance in the hand this reads *Franceschi*. It is **Francin** — and it is worth writing down rather than silently discarding, because it is **the same family Pietro De Franceschi married into**.

Pietro's first wife was «**Veniera Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel**». This groom's dead father is «**Pietro Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel**» — the identical patronymic, so **Veniera's brother**. The boy marrying here at nineteen is Veniera's nephew, and a first cousin of the Gio: Maria De Franceschi who married Lucia Bonassin in 1821.

**Francin is not Franceschi. But in Vodnjan the two families are one household deep in each other**, which is precisely why a name-match search on this parish would produce nonsense in both directions. *(doc — logged as a miss, and as a connection)*

rows.lab: The weaver a third time, and where the dispensations come from
rows.q:
**22** · 22 Febbraio **1830** · **№ domus 399**

**Testes** — **Pietro De Franceschi di Gio. — Tessitore**
Giacomo De Marchi, *Nunzolo di Chiesa*

*Dispensa dal 4° grado di Consanguinità dell'Ordinariato di **Pola**, 18 Feb.o 1830, № 97*
rows.why:
Third appearance for **Pietro De Franceschi di Gio., the weaver** — 1824 at Šišan, 1828 and now 1830 at home. He is a fixture.

And the right-hand column is quietly useful. The dispensations in this book are issued by the **Ordinariate of Pola**, and the banns can be waived by the **Imperial-Royal Circle Captaincy**. Vodnjan's paperwork ran to **Pola** for the church and to the Austrian civil administration for the state — which is where to write next for anything this register only alludes to. *(doc)*

rows.lab: 25 June 1830 — a fifth generation, out of a widow's second wedding
rows.q:
**20** · 25 Giugno **1830** · **№ domus 483**

**Sponsus** — **Domenico**, figlio delli furono giugali Domenico Fioranti fu Giorgio
e Mattea Bartolet q.m Ant.o, **vedovo in 2.do voto** della q.m Maria Ant.a Manzin
Cattolico · **d'Anni 53** · Vedovo

**Sponsa** — **Veniera**, figlia delli **furono giugali**
**Gio. Maria De Franceschi *fu Pietro*** **e Michiela Zambaletta fu Cristoforo**,
**vedova in 1.o voto** del q.m Domenico Pastrovicchio q.m Matteo
Cattolica · **d'Anni 49** · Vedova

**Testes** — D. Michiele Benedetto, Can.co Coffetti · Giacomo De Marchi, *Nunzolo di Chiesa*
rows.why:
Two years after she married her daughter off, **Veniera De Franceschi buries her husband and marries again at forty-nine** — and because a widow's remarriage is written out in full, the clerk names her parents. That single line does more than any other in the volume.

**«Gio. Maria De Franceschi *fu Pietro* e Michiela Zambaletta fu Cristoforo».**

The father who has been a bare name since March 1818 now has **a father of his own and a wife**. So the line in Vodnjan stands **five generations deep**, entirely off this one unindexed book:

· **Pietro De Franceschi** — dead before Gio. Maria was written down this way
· **Gio. Maria De Franceschi** × **Michiela Zambaletta fu Cristoforo** — both dead by 1830
· **Pietro** (b. c.1776) · **Cristoforo** · **Veniera** (b. c.1781)
· **Gio: Maria** (b. c.1799, m. Lucia Bonassin 1821) · **Michiela** (b. c.1800, m. 1826) · **Michiela Damiana Pastrovicchio** (b. c.1808, m. 1828)
· and the children baptised from 1822

**Michiela Zambaletta is the first woman named as a mother in this line at all**, and Veniera's age puts her own birth at about **1781** — which means the marriage of Gio. Maria and Michiela was in the 1770s, forty years before this register opens. *(doc for the entry; the generation dates are inf from stated ages)*

rows.lab: A fifth woman married out, and a shoemaker
rows.q:
**21** · 17 Novembre **1831** · **№ domus 266**

**Sponsus** — **Ant.o Gio.**, figlio di Fran.co Gorlato q.m Biaggio
e della **q.m Luigetta De Franceschi**, giugali · **d'Anni 23**

— and three months later —

**8** · 18 Febbraio **1832** · **№ domus 36**

**Testes** — **Giovanni De Franceschi q.m Pietro — *Calzolajo***
Giacomo De Marchi q.m Antonio, *Nunzolo di Chiesa*
rows.why:
**Luigetta De Franceschi** makes **five** women of the name married out of it and recoverable only through a child's wedding — after Domenica, Antonia Maria, Lucia and Veniera. She was dead by November 1831 and her son was twenty-three, so born about **1808**; she married a Gorlato.

And **Giovanni De Franceschi q.m Pietro** is a new man — **a shoemaker**. His «q.m Pietro» is the same formula as the **Pietro De Franceschi q.m Pietro, agricoltore**, who witnessed in 1824 and again in October 1831, and both sit beside **Bonetta**, daughter of «il fu Pietro De Franceschi q.m Dom.co», who married in 1823. On the dates and the patronymic they look like **three children of one Pietro** — the second Vodnjan line, the one descending from a Domenico. *(doc for each entry; the sibling grouping is inf)*

Which gives this small town, in one generation of one surname, **a priest, a ploughman, a weaver and a shoemaker** — and, from the other line, a farmer's household that could not sign its own name.

rows.lab: 17 July 1832 — a third wife named in the parents' generation
rows.q:
**28** · 17 Luglio **1832** · **№ domus 325**

**Sponsus** — **Domenico**, figlio delli furono giugali
**Pietro De Franceschi e Martina Civico q.m Domenico**,
**Vedovo della q.m Veniera De Rocchi fu Onorato**
Cattolico · **d'Anni 46** · Vedovo

**Sponsa** — Domenica, figlia delli furono giugali Andrea Biasiol q.m Ant.o
e Pasqua Marin q.m Dom.co, **vedova** del q.m Giuseppe fu Ant.o

**Testes** — Simone Marsanante fu Girolamo, *Civile*
Nicolò De Marchi q.m Domenico, *Possidente*
rows.why:
Two widowed people marrying in middle age, and because both are widowed the clerk writes everything out — which hands this archive **a couple it did not have**.

**Pietro De Franceschi × Martina Civico q.m Domenico**, both dead by 1832. Their son **Domenico** is forty-six, so born about **1786**; he had already been married once, to **Veniera De Rocchi fu Onorato**.

That is the **third** distinct wife now named in this generation of the surname at Vodnjan — after **Michiela Zambaletta** (wife of Gio. Maria) and **Domenica Manzin** (wife of the Pietro q.m Domenico whose daughter married in 1823).

**And it will not be forced into a shape.** This Pietro's wife is Martina Civico; the other Pietro's wife is Domenica Manzin. They may be one man twice married or two men of the same name — this parish has already produced four Pietros and two Cristoforos, and the register decides that question only when it decides to write a patronymic. It has not. *(doc for the entry; the relationship to the other Pietro is **open**)*

rows.lab: 1 December 1832 — Gio: Maria had a brother
rows.q:
**41** · 1 Dicembre **1832** · **№ domus 282**

**Sponsus** — **Domenico**, figlio di **Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria**
e della **q.m Veniera Francin q.m Domenico**, giugali
Cattolico · **d'Anni 29** · Celibe

**Sponsa** — Antonia, figlia del q.m Giovanni Del Carro q.m Pasquale
e di Bernardina Lugieri q.m Giacomo, giugali, **Vedova** · d'Anni 34

**Testes** — D. Giuseppe Del Ton, *Dottore* · **Gaudenzio Dalla Zonca, *nobile***
rows.why:
The same parents as the marriage of 9 June 1821: **Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria** and **Veniera Francin q.m Domenico**. So this is a **second son** of that couple — **Domenico, born about 1803**, four years behind his brother **Gio: Maria**.

The eldest Vodnjan line now runs:

· **Pietro** — named only in his son's patronymic
· **Gio. Maria** × **Michiela Zambaletta**, both dead by 1830
· **Pietro** (b. c.1776) × **Veniera Francin**, then Lorenza Tesser · **Cristoforo** · **Veniera** (b. c.1781)
· **Gio: Maria** (b. c.1799, m. 1821) · **Domenico** (b. c.1803, m. 1832) · **Michiela** (b. c.1800, m. 1826)

**Five generations and three of the fourth's siblings**, all of it out of a book no index touches. *(doc)*

rows.lab: 26 January 1833 — and this archive was wrong about him
rows.q:
**1** · 26 Gennajo **1833** · **№ domus 177**

*Subscriptio sacerdotis copulantis:*
**«D.n Stefano De Franceschi, De Parochi lic., li congiunse
e benedisse nella Chiesa Parrocchiale»**
rows.why:
**He married them himself.** *Joined them and blessed them in the parish church.*

This archive has said, on this page and in its commit messages, that Don Stefano appears **nineteen times as a witness and never once as the officiant**. That was true of every entry from 1819 to the end of 1832. It stops being true on **26 January 1833**, and it is corrected here rather than quietly amended.

What does not change is **how** he acts: «**De Parochi lic.**» — *by the parish priest's licence*. It is the same formula as the baptism of December 1816, «de Parocho licentia». Don Stefano is never the parson of Vodnjan; he is a priest of the chapter who steps in **when Giovanni Tromba licenses him to**, at a family baptism in 1816 and at the altar in 1833. Seventeen years apart, the register uses the same three words about him. *(doc)*

rows.lab: February 1833 — Giuseppe is dead, and the licence is routine
rows.q:
**13** · 12 Febbraio **1833** · **№ domus 332**
**Testes** — **Cristoforo De Franceschi *fu* Giuseppe — Tessitore**
*Subscriptio:* «**D.n Stefano De Franceschi, De Par. lic., li congiunse e benedisse
nella Chiesa della B. V. del Carmine**»

**14** · 13 Febbraio **1833** · **№ domus 437**
**Testes** — **Pietro De Franceschi fu Pietro — Agricoltore**
*Subscriptio:* «**D.n Pietro Bradamante, De Par. lic., li congiunse e benedisse
nella Chiesa della B. V. della Trovesa**»
rows.why:
Two consecutive days, and three things come out of them.

**Giuseppe De Franceschi is dead.** The weaver was «Cristoforo De Franceschi ***di*** Giuseppe» in March 1818 and again in November 1828. Here he is «***fu*** Giuseppe». The father of **the priest, the ploughman and the weaver** therefore died **between November 1828 and February 1833** — a date this archive did not have and can now put a bracket round. *(doc)*

**Don Stefano officiates a second time**, and not in the parish church: in the **church of the Blessed Virgin of Carmel**. With San Martino in 1829 and the Chiesa della B. V. della Trovesa the next day, Vodnjan is running marriages through **at least four churches**.

**And «De Par. lic.» is a formula, not a favour.** Yesterday this archive read it as the particular way Don Stefano was licensed by the parson — the same three words as the 1816 baptism. The very next entry uses them of **Don Pietro Bradamante**. So it is the register's **standard wording for any priest deputising for the parroco**, and the pattern this archive drew round Don Stefano is a pattern of the book, not of the man. *(doc — and a reading of it withdrawn the day after it was published)*

rows.lab: 27 July 1833 — the brothers get a mother, and she is a Tromba
rows.q:
**34** · 27 Luglio **1833** · **№ domus 324**

**Sponsa** — **Maria Francesca**, figlia **del fu Giuseppe De Franceschi q.m Pietro**
e di **Lucia Tromba q.m Cristoforo**, giugali
Cattolica · **d'Anni 28** · Celibe

**Testes** — Fran.co Davanzo fu Gio., *Trafficante*
**Sig.r Andrea Tromba fu Matteo, *Possidente Civile***
rows.why:
The household this archive has been circling since March 1818 — **Don Stefano the priest, Pietro the ploughman, Cristoforo the weaver, all «di Giuseppe»** — finally opens.

**«del fu Giuseppe De Franceschi q.m Pietro e di Lucia Tromba q.m Cristoforo».**

That is a **father for Giuseppe** (a Pietro), a **wife for Giuseppe** (Lucia Tromba), and a **fourth child**: Maria Francesca, twenty-eight, so born about **1805**. And Giuseppe is «*del fu*» — dead — which sits exactly inside the bracket the weaver's own patronymic gave: after November 1828, before February 1833.

**And the mother is a Tromba.** The parish priest who signs the foot of every page of this book is **Giovanni Tromba, Doctor of Sacred Theology, parroco and Provost of the Chapter**. One of the two witnesses here is **Andrea Tromba, *Possidente Civile***.

That reframes the whole household. A family of a ploughman and a weaver who cannot write their own names produced **a priest of the chapter** — and their mother came from the family that held the parish. It also explains the formula that has run through this reading from the start: Don Stefano acting «**de Parocho licentia**», by the leave of a parson who was, in all likelihood, **his own kinsman**. *(doc for the entry; that this Giuseppe is the brothers' father is **inf** — same town, same generation, death inside the same bracket — and the Tromba kinship is **inf**, on a shared surname in a small town)*

The line now stands:

· **Pietro De Franceschi** — named only as Giuseppe's dead father
· **Giuseppe** × **Lucia Tromba q.m Cristoforo** — Giuseppe dead 1828×1833
· **Don Stefano**, priest · **Pietro**, agricoltore · **Cristoforo**, tessitore · **Maria Francesca**, b. c.1805

rows.lab: The death register, opened
rows.q:
**54** · 11 Marzo **1829** · **№ domus 325**
«**Maria, figlia di Stefano De Franceschi e di Bonetta Vellico q.m Antonio, giugali**»
— *LIBER DEFUNCTORUM in Ecclesia S. Blasii Adignani*
rows.why:
The third book on the film. **Deaths 1815–1833 run from about image 471 to 575**, in a Latin-headed ruling — *Tempus mortis · Nrus domus · Nomen defuncti · Religio · Sexus · Aetas · Morbus seu causa mortis* — about thirteen entries a page, twenty-six an opening, and roughly six images to the year.

**It is not indexed either.** A query for De Franceschi deaths across 1826–1836 in the whole of Croatia returns **eight dated records**, none of them from this parish.

The first entry read out of it belongs to **Stefano De Franceschi and Bonetta Vellico** — one of the eight households this archive reconstructed from the baptism index months ago. Their daughter **Maria died on 11 March 1829 at house 325**. The household had children recorded 1819–1829; now it has a burial too, and a house number.

What this book is being read for: **Giuseppe De Franceschi**, whose death his sons' patronymics bracket to **between November 1828 and February 1833**, and who should therefore be somewhere in images 546–575. *(doc)*

rows.lab: The death book gives two households their dead
rows.q:
**54** · 11 Marzo **1829** · **№ domus 325**
«Maria, figlia di **Stefano De Franceschi** e di **Bonetta Vellico q.m Antonio**, giugali»

**96** · 23 Luglio **1829** · **№ domus 48**
«Pietro, figlio di **Dom.co De Franceschi q.m Pietro** e di **Zacchera Cerlon di Franc.o**, giugali»
rows.why:
Two of the eight households reconstructed from the baptism index now have a **burial** and a **house number** — and the second has something better.

«**Dom.co De Franceschi *q.m Pietro***». The baptism index gave this household as a bare pair of names, *Domenico × Zacchera Cerlon*, with children 1817–1833. The death of their son **Pietro on 23 July 1829 at house 48** names Domenico's **own dead father: a Pietro**.

That is a **fifth Pietro** in this parish, or one of the four already known — and the register does not say which. What it does say is that the household has a generation above it, which the baptism book never showed. *(doc)*

rows.lab: 14 February 1830 — Giuseppe, found, and the bracket closes exactly
rows.q:
**27** · 14 Febrajo **1830** · **№ domus 324**

«**Giuseppe De Franceschi q.m Pietro era ammogliato
con Lucia Tromba fu Cristoforo**»
Cattolico · Maschio · **d'anni 72**
*Morbus seu causa mortis:* **Vizio organico di petto**
*Sacramenti:* **senza assistenza spirituale per morte improvvisa**

— and five months later —

**77** · 13 Luglio **1830** · **№ domus 501**

«**Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro era Moglie
di Alviso Birattan q.m Sabà**»
Cattolica · Femmina · **d'anni 70** · *Ascite universale*
rows.why:
**The father of the priest, the ploughman and the weaver.** This archive had never seen a date for him — it had a **bracket**, derived from nothing but how his sons were written: «*di* Giuseppe» in November 1828, «*fu* Giuseppe» in February 1833.

The register gives **14 February 1830**. Inside the bracket, and the bracket was right.

And it gives four things the marriages never could. He was **seventy-two**, so born about **1758**. He died **at house 324** — the house his daughter Maria Francesca would marry out of three years later. The cause was an **organic defect of the chest**. And the sacraments column, which is usually a formula, says he **died suddenly, with no priest**: «*senza assistenza spirituale per morte improvvisa*».

His son was a priest of that parish, licensed by the parroco to baptise and to marry. **Don Stefano did not get to his own father.** *(doc)*

**And then, five months later, Lucia.** «**Lucia De Franceschi *q.m Pietro***», wife of Alviso Birattan q.m Sabà, dead of dropsy at **seventy**, so born about **1760**. She is the woman whose three daughters married out of the name in 1821, 1824 and 1825, and who existed here only because those weddings named their mother.

**Both are «q.m Pietro». Born about 1758 and about 1760, in one small town, dying five months apart.** They are almost certainly **brother and sister** — which joins Giuseppe's household to Lucia's, and puts a **Pietro De Franceschi born around 1730** behind both. *(doc for both entries; the sibling reading is **inf**, and it is the strongest inference this reading has produced)*

rows.lab: 11 September 1830 — house 325 gets its family
rows.q:
**94** · 11 Settembre **1830** · **№ domus 325**

«**Bonetta Vellico q.m Antonio, Moglie di
Stefano De Franceschi *di* Domenico q.m Pietro**»
Cattolica · Femmina · **d'anni 57** · *Tisi polmonare*
rows.why:
Eighteen months after her daughter Maria died in the same house, **Bonetta Vellico dies at house 325** of pulmonary consumption, aged fifty-seven — so born about **1773**.

And the clerk writes her husband out three generations deep: «**Stefano De Franceschi *di* Domenico *q.m* Pietro**». Note the two different words. ***Di*** Domenico — **his father was alive** in September 1830. ***Q.m*** Pietro — his grandfather was not.

So a third Vodnjan line stands: **Pietro → Domenico → Stefano**, with Domenico still living.

**And house 325 is now theirs.** This archive flagged that number two days ago because it also appears against **Domenico De Franceschi, forty-six, son of a Pietro and Martina Civico**, remarrying in July **1832**. The house is Stefano and Bonetta's; the Domenico who married out of it two years later shares a grandfather's name with Stefano's own father.

**The connection is now likely rather than merely possible — and the exact link is still open.** On the stated ages the 1832 Domenico (born about 1786) is too young to be Stefano's father, so the readings on the table are: two brothers of one name, an uncle, or an age the register got wrong. **This archive is not going to pick one.** *(doc for the entry; the join is inf, and which join it is remains open)*
